subject: Copywriting
title: Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind
description: A 60-second lesson on Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind.

hook.text: In 1969, Ries and Trout argued that products don't matter—what matters is the position in the buyer's mind.

buildup.text: Avis was losing to Hertz. Instead of claiming superiority, they said 'We're #2. We try harder.' It worked.

discovery.text: Positioning meant owning a mental slot. Volvo owns 'safety.' FedEx owns 'overnight.' Coke owns 'original.'

twist.text: You can't own a position someone else holds. Pepsi never beat Coke on 'original.' So they chose 'youth.'

climax.text: Every brand strategy today starts with positioning. It's the single most influential concept in marketing.

punchline.text: Products live on shelves. Brands live in minds.

quiz.question: What was Avis's famous positioning strategy?
